subject: Music Production
title: Mutt Lange's Arena Rock Sound
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Mutt Lange's Arena Rock Sound.

hook.text: Robert 'Mutt' Lange spent months in the studio obsessively layering vocals and guitar tracks.

buildup.text: He recorded dozens of takes for every vocal line, then stacked them to create a massive chorus.

discovery.text: This painstaking approach produced the enormous sound of AC/DC's 'Back in Black' album.

twist.text: Lange's perfectionism drove some artists to exhaustion, with albums taking over a year to finish.

climax.text: His method defined arena rock and made 'Back in Black' one of the best-selling albums ever.

punchline.text: Obsessive layering built rock's biggest albums.

quiz.question: What was distinctive about Mutt Lange's production method?
options: Recording everything live in one take
Obsessively layering dozens of vocal and guitar takes
